circuit: H on every qubit, measure every qubit into c[i]; optimization_level 0; initial layout = identity; A and B submitted back to back
packing: per shot c0..c(n-1), c0 = rightmost char; shots concatenated in returned order; MSB-first; partial byte dropped

channel_rule.why: the r1 rule unchanged: a channel is broken only when max(p0,p1) exceeds 0.707 after the 99 % margin; biased-but-usable channels are charged in the per-channel accounting

software.where: tools/qrng of the public repo (the published module and checker)

calibration: vendor properties snapshot (readout_error per qubit, last_update) before job A and after job B; K7 and K8 are scored only if the two last_update values are equal, otherwise reported as UNMEASURED (not re-scored)

per_job (A and B each).K1: module ACCEPTS the block under policy exclude (health tests 0 failures, h_mcv >= 6.0, |lag1| <= 5/sqrt(N), no replay)
per_job (A and B each).K4: buyer checker (qrng_fuggetlen, --expect-rows 1) PASS, accounting and exclusion recomputed
per_job (A and B each).K5: excluded channels between 0 and 4 (r0 under the rule excludes 1, r1 0)
per_job (A and B each).K6: per-channel accounting h_acc in [6.731, 8.0] (r0 h_acc 7.231, r1 7.300; floor = min - 0.5 bit)

predictions.K7: Pearson r of per-qubit p(1) between A and B >= 0.622 (two jobs minutes apart under ONE vendor calibration; expected r 0.872 if the per-qubit bias is constant within a calibration (var_bias pooled over r0 and r1 / (var_bias + var_noise)); 0.25 margin as in r1; below the floor = the bias is not even stable over minutes = uncalibratable drift above shot noise)
predictions.K8: r(A,B) > r(A,r1) > r(A,r0) (the bias correlation falls with calibration age (minutes, ~2 days, ~5 days); day-scale reference r(r0,r1) = 0.356)
predictions.K9: Pearson r of the vendor readout-error table, snapshot before A vs r1 >= 0.9 (the vendor's readout-error table was stable r0<->r1 (r 0.954); r2 (snapshot before A) vs r1)

interpretation: K1-K6 on both jobs = the published module and checker run end to end twice more on a real source. K7 is the physics claim r1 left open: the per-qubit bias is stable within one calibration (minutes) even though it moves between days. K7 red = the bias is drift above shot noise that no calibration can predict, so the module's channel test must work from the current block only (it already does) - this is then stated on the page. K8 orders the correlation by calibration age; K9 checks the vendor table is as stable as before. Statistics cannot certify quantumness; the receipt stays 'statistical'. A failure is reported as measured.
